titleEn: Children who grow up in poverty are 5 times more likely to be poor young adults: new study
titleZh: 新研究：童年贫困者成年初期陷入贫困的可能性高出五倍
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: About 757,000 Australian children aged under 15 lived in poverty in 2022-23 – more than all the people living in cities of Geelong, Newcastle and Wollongong combined.
paragraphs.zh: 2022-23年度，约有75. 7万名15岁以下的澳大利亚儿童生活在贫困中--超过了生活在基隆、纽卡斯尔和卧龙岗等城市的所有人口的总和。

paragraphs.en: That’s about one in six Australian children, according to the latest estimates from the Australian Council of Social Service (ACOSS) and UNSW Sydney.
paragraphs.zh: 根据澳大利亚社会服务理事会和悉尼新南威尔士大学的最新估计，这大约是六分之一的澳大利亚儿童。

paragraphs.en: But what happens to these children as they grow older? Do the disadvantages of growing up below the poverty line disappear as they finish school, find jobs and establish their own households?
paragraphs.zh: 但是，当这些孩子长大后会发生什么呢？当他们完成学业、找到工作并建立自己的家庭时，在贫困线以下长大的不利条件是否会消失呢？

paragraphs.en: Our research, recently published in The Economic Record, suggests childhood poverty casts a long shadow, affecting young Australians well into their 20s and 30s.
paragraphs.zh: 我们最近发表在《经济记录》上的研究表明，童年贫困投下了长长的阴影，影响着20多岁和30多岁的澳大利亚年轻人。

paragraphs.en: Lasting effects of a poor childhood
paragraphs.zh: 贫穷童年的持久影响

paragraphs.en: We used data from the Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia (HILDA) Survey, which has followed Australian households since 2001.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用了澳大利亚家庭、收入和劳动力动态调查（HILDA）的数据，该调查自2001年以来一直跟踪澳大利亚家庭。

paragraphs.en: We examined 2,205 people whose childhood household incomes were observed in at least three years, and whose incomes were known at least once again from age 24. This allowed us to examine whether growing up in poverty was associated with an increased risk of experiencing poverty as adults, aged 24 to 35.
paragraphs.zh: 我们调查了2，205名儿童时期家庭收入至少在三年内被观察过，并且从24岁起至少再次知道收入的人。这使我们能够研究在贫困中长大是否与经历贫困的风险增加有关。作为成年人，24岁至35岁。

paragraphs.en: Australia does not have an official poverty line. So we defined poverty using a relative income measure, widely used in international research. This takes into account household disposable income (after taxes and government payments, such as family tax benefits) and is adjusted for household size.
paragraphs.zh: 澳大利亚没有官方的贫困线，因此我们使用国际研究中广泛使用的相对收入衡量标准来定义贫困。该标准考虑了家庭可支配收入（税后和政府支付，如家庭税收优惠），并根据家庭规模进行了调整。

paragraphs.en: In dollar terms, the poverty line we were looking at sits at about A$72,000 for a couple with two children, and about $55,000 for a single parent with two children.
paragraphs.zh: 以美元计算，我们所看到的贫困线对于一对有两个孩子的夫妇来说大约是72，000澳元，对于一个有两个孩子的单亲父母来说大约是55，000澳元。

paragraphs.en: We found children growing up below the poverty line had a 22.4 percentage points higher risk of living in poverty in their 20s and early 30s than those who grew up in households with incomes between 150% and 200% of the poverty line.
paragraphs.zh: 我们发现，在贫困线以下长大的儿童在20多岁和30岁出头时生活在贫困中的风险比那些在收入在贫困线150%至200%之间的家庭中长大的儿童高出22.4%。

paragraphs.en: To be clear, 200% of the poverty line, the upper limit of the childhood income of the reference group, is still not even close to being wealthy. It’s simply the median income: about $144,000 for a couple with two children.
paragraphs.zh: 需要明确的是，贫困线的200%，也就是参照组儿童收入的上限，还远远没有达到富裕水平。这只是收入的中位数：一对有两个孩子的夫妇的收入约为144，000美元。

paragraphs.en: What this means is that Australians who grow up poor face a 27% risk of being in poverty in early adulthood, in contrast to just 5% in the reference group. That’s more than five times the risk.
paragraphs.zh: 这意味着，在贫困中长大的澳大利亚人在成年早期面临27%的贫困风险，而对照组只有5%。这是风险的五倍多。

paragraphs.en: We also looked at others who grew up in near-poverty, with household incomes between 100% and 150% of the poverty line, or roughly $72,000 to $108,000 for a couple with two children. They also had a higher poverty rate in early-adulthood: 8.7 percentage points higher than children from the reference group.
paragraphs.zh: 我们还研究了其他在接近贫困的环境中长大的人，他们的家庭收入在贫困线的100%到150%之间，或者说一对有两个孩子的夫妇的家庭收入在72，000美元到108，000美元之间。他们在成年早期的贫困率也更高：比参照组的孩子高出8.7个百分点。

paragraphs.en: By contrast, we found no statistically significant differences in early adulthood poverty between the income group just below the median and those who grew up in households with higher incomes.
paragraphs.zh: 相比之下，我们发现，在收入低于中位数的人群和那些在收入较高的家庭中长大的人之间，成年早期的贫困没有统计学上的显著差异。

paragraphs.en: A ‘double whammy’ for kids from single-parent families
paragraphs.zh: 单亲家庭孩子的“双重打击”

paragraphs.en: Australia has 1.2 million single parent families. Children in those families are especially vulnerable to poverty persisting into early adulthood.
paragraphs.zh: 澳大利亚有120万个单亲家庭，这些家庭的儿童特别容易陷入贫困，并一直持续到成年早期。

paragraphs.en: According to 2026 ACOSS–UNSW research, 37% of children in sole-parent families were living in poverty in 2022–23, compared with 11% of children in partnered families.
paragraphs.zh: 根据2026年ACOSS-UNSW的研究，2022-23年单亲家庭中37%的儿童生活在贫困中，而伴侣家庭中的儿童则为11%。

paragraphs.en: Low-income single-parent families face compounding pressures: even beyond obvious financial pressures, one parent also has to carry out all the unpaid work of child care and household tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 低收入单亲家庭面临着多重压力：即使在明显的经济压力之外，父母一方还必须承担所有无报酬的儿童保育和家务劳动。

paragraphs.en: Not only are children in single-parent families more likely to experience poverty, our research showed that poverty is more persistent into adulthood, likely because of those compounding pressures. It’s a double whammy.
paragraphs.zh: 单亲家庭的孩子不仅更有可能经历贫困，我们的研究表明，贫困更容易持续到成年，可能是因为这些复合压力。这是一个双重打击。

paragraphs.en: In August 2025, Swinburne University researchers surveyed 2,590 Australian single parents, who were mostly women.
paragraphs.zh: 2025年8月，斯威本大学的研究人员对2,590名澳大利亚单亲父母进行了调查，其中大部分是女性。

paragraphs.en: They found almost four out of five single mothers (78%) spent “a lot” or “almost all” of their time worrying about or planning for their family’s financial wellbeing. As one respondent said:
paragraphs.zh: 他们发现，近五分之四（78%）的单身母亲花了“很多”或“几乎所有”时间担心或计划家庭的财务状况。

paragraphs.en: I need more money. The financial stress feels untenable.
paragraphs.zh: 我需要更多的钱。经济压力太大了。

paragraphs.en: What makes poverty persist into adulthood?
paragraphs.zh: 是什么让贫困持续到成年？

paragraphs.en: We examined several possible reasons why poverty is more likely to last into later life. These included educational attainment, reduced employment, lower rates of partnering and poorer health.
paragraphs.zh: 我们研究了贫困更可能持续到晚年的几个可能原因，包括教育程度、就业率下降、伴侣比例降低和健康状况较差。

paragraphs.en: We found people who grew up in more disadvantaged households were generally less likely to complete post-school qualifications, be employed or live with a partner.
paragraphs.zh: 我们发现，在弱势家庭长大的人通常不太可能完成毕业后的资格，就业或与伴侣生活在一起。

paragraphs.en: They were also more likely to be single parents. Some health measures were also associated with childhood economic circumstances.
paragraphs.zh: 他们也更可能是单亲父母。一些健康措施也与儿童时期的经济状况有关。

paragraphs.en: These adult outcomes are themselves associated with poverty risk. But even when we accounted for them, the association between childhood poverty and early-adulthood poverty remained substantial.
paragraphs.zh: 这些成年后的结果本身就与贫困风险有关，但即使我们考虑了这些因素，童年贫困与成年早期贫困之间的关联仍然很大。

paragraphs.en: What can we do about it?
paragraphs.zh: 我们能做些什么呢？

paragraphs.en: Our research doesn’t isolate a single cause of childhood poverty. But our findings do strongly suggest policies focused on reducing poverty in families with children can deliver lasting benefits.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的研究并没有孤立出儿童贫困的单一原因，但我们的研究结果确实有力地表明，专注于减少有孩子家庭贫困的政策可以带来持久的好处。

paragraphs.en: To significantly reduce adult poverty, we need more focus on directly reducing economic hardship in families with children, especially those from low-income single-parent families.
paragraphs.zh: 为了大幅度减少成人贫困，我们需要更加注重直接减少有子女家庭的经济困难，特别是那些来自低收入单亲家庭的家庭。

paragraphs.en: In 2023, the Albanese government boosted financial support for low-income single parents, raising the age cut-off for the Parenting Payment (Single) until the youngest child turns 14. That change was expected to help at least 57,000 single primary carers, who were mostly women (91%).
paragraphs.zh: 2023年，阿尔巴尼亚政府增加了对低收入单亲父母的财政支持，提高了养育费（单身）的年龄截止日期，直到最小的孩子年满14岁。这一变化预计将帮助至少57，000名单身初级照顾者，其中大多数是女性（91%）。

paragraphs.en: But more is still required, such as targeted increases to Family Tax Benefit Part A payments.
paragraphs.zh: 但仍需要更多，例如有针对性地增加家庭税收福利A部分的支付。

paragraphs.en: And if we want to track the success of policy changes in reducing long-term poverty, we need better evidence. That means more long-term studies, following individuals over their lives from kids to adults.
paragraphs.zh: 如果我们想跟踪政策变化在减少长期贫困方面的成功，我们需要更好的证据。这意味着更多的长期研究，跟踪从儿童到成年人的个人生活。

paragraphs.en: Then we would be able to better identify the key factors keeping Australians locked into poverty for decades – or helping them escape it.
paragraphs.zh: 这样，我们就能够更好地确定使澳大利亚人陷入贫困数十年的关键因素-或帮助他们摆脱贫困。
